manifest.title: Explicit Subcubic Expanders and Linear Treewidth

inputs.abstract:
We construct [arbitrarily large subcubic expanders](Lax920634.ExpanderExistence.html)
and deduce [subcubic graphs of linear treewidth](Lax920634.TreewidthExistence.html).
The deterministic construction uses a fixed seed, zig-zag products, and path
replacement. A [uniform word-RAM algorithm](Lax920634.LinearConstruction.html)
outputs an $N$-vertex member in $O(N)$ time using $O(\log(N+1))$-bit words.
The fixed constants are enormous.

concepts.title: The Constructor Meets the Requested Order
concepts.description:
For every requested order $n$, the selector produces a graph with at least
$n$ vertices and at most $2dD^4(n+1)$ vertices. Thus the polynomial-time
algorithm constructs arbitrarily large graphs with only a fixed-factor
overshoot. Here $D=120^{5760000}$ and $d=D^2$ are fixed.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown: Both bounds concern the exact level used by the binary table constructor.

title: The Constructor Meets the Requested Order
type: lemma

For every requested order $n$, the selector produces a graph with at least

namespace Lax920634.ConstructionSize

open ZigZagConstruction GraphEncoding SeedSearch

/-- The specified size selector meets the request with a fixed linear upper bound. -/
axiom size_bounds (n : ℕ) :
  n ≤ order (selectedLevel n) ∧
  order (selectedLevel n) ≤
    (2 * degree * seedDegree ^ 4) * (n + 1)

end Lax920634.ConstructionSize

concepts.title: Edge Expansion and Subcubic Graphs
concepts.description:
The edge boundary of a vertex set $S$ consists of the edges with one endpoint
in $S$ and one outside. A finite graph has edge expansion at least $h$ if
$|\partial S|\ge h|S|$ whenever $|S|\le |V|/2$. A graph is subcubic if
every vertex has at most three neighbors.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Boundary edges are represented by ordered pairs with the first endpoint in
$S$ and the second outside, so each undirected boundary edge is counted once.
`Set.ncard` avoids imposing decidability on mathematical predicates; every
set counted here is finite. Expansion constants are rational numbers.

concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card
import Mathlib.Data.Rat.Defs

/-!
---
title: Edge Expansion and Subcubic Graphs
type: definition
---
The edge boundary of a vertex set $S$ consists of the edges with one endpoint
in $S$ and one outside. A finite graph has edge expansion at least $h$ if
$|\partial S|\ge h|S|$ whenever $|S|\le |V|/2$. A graph is subcubic if
every vertex has at most three neighbors.

# Formalization notes

Boundary edges are represented by ordered pairs with the first endpoint in
$S$ and the second outside, so each undirected boundary edge is counted once.
`Set.ncard` avoids imposing decidability on mathematical predicates; every
set counted here is finite. Expansion constants are rational numbers.
-/

namespace Lax920634.EdgeExpansion

/-- Boundary edges oriented from the set to its complement, each counted once. -/
def edgeBoundary {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : Set V) : Set (V × V) :=
  {e | e.1 ∈ S ∧ e.2 ∉ S ∧ G.Adj e.1 e.2}

/-- Every vertex set of size at most half the graph has at least `h` times
its size in boundary edges. -/
def HasEdgeExpansionAtLeast {V : Type} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (h : ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set V, 2 * S.ncard ≤ Fintype.card V →
    h * (S.ncard : ℚ) ≤ ((edgeBoundary G S).ncard : ℚ)

/-- Every vertex has at most three distinct neighbors. -/
def IsSubcubic {V : Type} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∀ v, (G.neighborSet v).ncard ≤ 3

end Lax920634.EdgeExpansion

concepts.title: Arbitrarily Large Subcubic Expanders
concepts.description:
For every size threshold there is a finite simple subcubic graph above that
threshold with edge expansion at least $1/(8d)$, where $d=D^2$ is fixed.
The witnesses are generated by the specified deterministic polynomial-time
construction.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Graphs use canonical carriers `Fin n`. The threshold may be exceeded;
the level-selection algorithm keeps the excess within a fixed constant factor.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax920634.ZigZagConstruction

/-!
---
title: Arbitrarily Large Subcubic Expanders
type: theorem
---
For every size threshold there is a finite simple subcubic graph above that
threshold with edge expansion at least $1/(8d)$, where $d=D^2$ is fixed.
The witnesses are generated by the specified deterministic polynomial-time
construction.

# Formalization notes

Graphs use canonical carriers `Fin n`. The threshold may be exceeded;
the level-selection algorithm keeps the excess within a fixed constant factor.
-/

namespace Lax920634.ExpanderExistence

open ZigZagConstruction EdgeExpansion

/-- There are arbitrarily large finite simple subcubic expanders with one fixed constant. -/
axiom exists_subcubic_expander (lower : ℕ) :
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), lower ≤ n ∧
    IsSubcubic G ∧
    HasEdgeExpansionAtLeast G (1 / (8 * (degree : ℚ)))

end Lax920634.ExpanderExistence

  Exists fun n =>
    Exists fun G =>
      And (instLENat.le lower n)
        (And (Lax920634.EdgeExpansion.IsSubcubic G)
          (Lax920634.EdgeExpansion.HasEdgeExpansionAtLeast G
            (instHDiv.hDiv 1 (instHMul.hMul 8 Lax920634.ZigZagConstruction.degree.cast))))

concepts.title: Edge Expansion Forces Linear Treewidth
concepts.description:
For a positive integer $d$, every finite subcubic graph with edge expansion
at least $1/(8d)$ satisfies
$|V|\le(24d+1)(\operatorname{tw}(G)+1)$.

If every component after deleting $X$ has size at most $|V|/2$, summing the
expansion inequalities over components gives
$|V\setminus X|\le24d|X|$. Thus a smaller deletion leaves a component
containing more than half the graph. These large connected sets form a
bramble. A bag of every tree decomposition hits the bramble, giving the bound.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Treewidth is the registered definition from `Lax228581.Treewidth`.
The additive one is necessary for graphs of treewidth zero. Empty graphs
are included. Natural-number multiplication avoids rounding conventions.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax920634.EdgeExpansion
import Lax228581.Treewidth

/-!
---
title: Edge Expansion Forces Linear Treewidth
type: lemma
---
For a positive integer $d$, every finite subcubic graph with edge expansion
at least $1/(8d)$ satisfies
$|V|\le(24d+1)(\operatorname{tw}(G)+1)$.

If every component after deleting $X$ has size at most $|V|/2$, summing the
expansion inequalities over components gives
$|V\setminus X|\le24d|X|$. Thus a smaller deletion leaves a component
containing more than half the graph. These large connected sets form a
bramble. A bag of every tree decomposition hits the bramble, giving the bound.

# Formalization notes

Treewidth is the registered definition from `Lax228581.Treewidth`.
The additive one is necessary for graphs of treewidth zero. Empty graphs
are included. Natural-number multiplication avoids rounding conventions.
-/

namespace Lax920634.ExpansionTreewidth

open EdgeExpansion Lax228581.Treewidth

/-- Uniform expansion in a subcubic graph gives a linear lower bound on treewidth. -/
axiom order_le_treewidth {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d)
    (hdegree : IsSubcubic G)
    (hex : HasEdgeExpansionAtLeast G (1 / (8 * (d : ℚ)))) :
  n ≤ (24 * d + 1) * (treewidth G + 1)

end Lax920634.ExpansionTreewidth

statements.signature:
order_le_treewidth : ∀ {n : Nat} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (d : Nat),
  instLTNat.lt 0 d →
    Lax920634.EdgeExpansion.IsSubcubic G →
      Lax920634.EdgeExpansion.HasEdgeExpansionAtLeast G (instHDiv.hDiv 1 (instHMul.hMul 8 d.cast)) →
        instLENat.le n
          (instHMul.hMul (instHAdd.hAdd (instHMul.hMul 24 d) 1) (instHAdd.hAdd (Lax228581.Treewidth.treewidth G) 1))
statements.doc: Uniform expansion in a subcubic graph gives a linear lower bound on treewidth.

concepts.title: The Explicit Subcubic Family Expands
concepts.description:
Put $D=120^{5760000}$ and $d=D^2$. Every specified graph $H_k$ has edge
expansion at least $1/(8d)$, uniformly in the level.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The constant depends only on the fixed seed degree, not on the graph order.
The proof combines the zig-zag spectral bound with path replacement and
checks the canonical vertex numbering.

/-!
---
title: The Explicit Subcubic Family Expands
type: lemma
---
Put $D=120^{5760000}$ and $d=D^2$. Every specified graph $H_k$ has edge
expansion at least $1/(8d)$, uniformly in the level.

# Formalization notes

The constant depends only on the fixed seed degree, not on the graph order.
The proof combines the zig-zag spectral bound with path replacement and
checks the canonical vertex numbering.

namespace Lax920634.ExplicitExpansion

open ZigZagConstruction EdgeExpansion

/-- The specified deterministic family has a uniform positive edge-expansion constant. -/
axiom expansion (k : ℕ) : HasEdgeExpansionAtLeast
  (graph k) (1 / (8 * (degree : ℚ)))

end Lax920634.ExplicitExpansion

concepts.title: The Explicit Family Has Linear Treewidth
concepts.description:
The specified graphs satisfy
$N_k\le(24d+1)(\operatorname{tw}(H_k)+1)$, where $d=D^2$ is the fixed
regular tower degree. Hence sufficiently large members have treewidth at
least $N_k/(48d+2)$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The expansion and treewidth claims refer to the same computable graph.
The existence theorem below absorbs the additive one by choosing a large
enough size request.

open ZigZagConstruction Lax228581.Treewidth

/-- The specified graph order is bounded linearly by treewidth plus one. -/
axiom linear_treewidth (k : ℕ) : order k ≤

    (treewidth (graph k) + 1)

end Lax920634.ExplicitTreewidth

concepts.title: Selecting and Encoding the Constructed Graphs
concepts.description:
Given a requested order $n$ in unary, start at the smallest tower member and
advance while its regular-graph order is below $2n$. At most $2n$ advances
suffice. After path replacement this selects a graph of order between $n$
and a fixed constant times $n+1$.

The output lists the paired-port destination of every vertex, in numerical
order. A destination is recorded as its base vertex and its port, both in
unary. The two possible path neighbors follow directly from the row number.
This table determines the entire simple graph, including the removal of loops
and duplicate edges.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The binary serialization uses balanced brackets: `false` opens a list and
`true` closes one. A Boolean is an empty list for `false` and a list containing
one empty list for `true`. Records are pairs of unary Boolean words. The
whole table is a list of these records. The format is unambiguous; its unary
coordinates increase output size only polynomially.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax920634.ZigZagConstruction
import Mathlib.Data.List.Basic

/-!
---
title: Selecting and Encoding the Constructed Graphs
type: definition
---
Given a requested order $n$ in unary, start at the smallest tower member and
advance while its regular-graph order is below $2n$. At most $2n$ advances
suffice. After path replacement this selects a graph of order between $n$
and a fixed constant times $n+1$.

The output lists the paired-port destination of every vertex, in numerical
order. A destination is recorded as its base vertex and its port, both in
unary. The two possible path neighbors follow directly from the row number.
This table determines the entire simple graph, including the removal of loops
and duplicate edges.

# Formalization notes

The binary serialization uses balanced brackets: `false` opens a list and
`true` closes one. A Boolean is an empty list for `false` and a list containing
one empty list for `true`. Records are pairs of unary Boolean words. The
whole table is a list of these records. The format is unambiguous; its unary
coordinates increase output size only polynomially.
-/

namespace Lax920634.GraphEncoding

open SeedSearch ZigZagConstruction

/-- The bounded level-selection loop, carrying the level and current regular order. -/
def levelAfter (b n : ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ × ℕ → ℕ × ℕ
  | 0, p => p
  | j + 1, p =>
      let q := levelAfter b n j p
      if q.2 < 2 * n then (q.1 + 1, q.2 * b) else q

/-- The level selected for a requested order, after at most `2*n` advances. -/
def selectedLevel (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (levelAfter (seedDegree ^ 4) n (2 * n) (0, seedDegree ^ 4)).1

/-- A Boolean serialized as an empty or singleton-empty bracketed list. -/
def encodeBit (b : Bool) : List Bool :=
  if b then [false, false, true, true] else [false, true]

/-- Serialize a Boolean word as a bracketed list of encoded Booleans. -/
def encodeWord (w : List Bool) : List Bool := false :: (w.flatMap encodeBit ++ [true])

/-- Serialize a pair of natural coordinates, each represented in unary. -/
def encodeRecord (p : ℕ × ℕ) : List Bool :=
  false :: (encodeWord (List.replicate p.1 true) ++
    encodeWord (List.replicate p.2 true) ++ [true])

/-- The paired-port destination of each vertex, in canonical row order. -/
def records (k : ℕ) : List (ℕ × ℕ) :=
  (List.range (order k)).map fun j =>
    rotation k (j / degree, j % degree)

/-- The binary table encoding of the entire subcubic graph at a specified level. -/
def encoding (k : ℕ) : List Bool := false :: ((records k).flatMap encodeRecord ++ [true])

/-- The specified deterministic graph construction on a unary size request. -/
def construct (input : List Bool) : List Bool := encoding (selectedLevel input.length)

end Lax920634.GraphEncoding

concepts.title: Linear-Time Construction on the Word RAM
concepts.description:
One fixed deterministic word-RAM program constructs the specified subcubic
graphs in linear time in their output order. The program receives a requested
order as one word and outputs the complete word-sized matching table.

There are constants $c_t,c_w>0$ such that its actual instruction count is at
most $c_t(N+1)$ at every word width satisfying $c_w(N+1)\le2^w$, where $N$ is
the selected graph's order. Consequently $O(\log(N+1))$-bit words suffice.
The program and constants are chosen before the request and the word width.
The proof supplies $c_t=25381$ and $c_w=128$.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Materialize the fixed seed and build the rotation tables from the bottom up.
Each new row uses a constant number of lookups in the seed and preceding table.
Geometric growth bounds the total number of rows by a constant multiple of
$N$. A verified compiler transfers this bound to actual registered RAM
instructions, including initialization and output. The fixed seed and
level-zero table are program literals determined by the specified seed scan;
writing these literals into RAM is charged. No data depending on the request
or word width are built into the program.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax920634.WordEncoding
import Lax808846.RamComputes

/-!
---
title: Linear-Time Construction on the Word RAM
type: theorem
---
One fixed deterministic word-RAM program constructs the specified subcubic
graphs in linear time in their output order. The program receives a requested
order as one word and outputs the complete word-sized matching table.

There are constants $c_t,c_w>0$ such that its actual instruction count is at
most $c_t(N+1)$ at every word width satisfying $c_w(N+1)\le2^w$, where $N$ is
the selected graph's order. Consequently $O(\log(N+1))$-bit words suffice.
The program and constants are chosen before the request and the word width.
The proof supplies $c_t=25381$ and $c_w=128$.

# Proof strategy

Materialize the fixed seed and build the rotation tables from the bottom up.
Each new row uses a constant number of lookups in the seed and preceding table.
Geometric growth bounds the total number of rows by a constant multiple of
$N$. A verified compiler transfers this bound to actual registered RAM
instructions, including initialization and output. The fixed seed and
level-zero table are program literals determined by the specified seed scan;
writing these literals into RAM is charged. No data depending on the request
or word width are built into the program.
-/

namespace Lax920634.LinearConstruction

open ZigZagConstruction Lax808846.Ram
open GraphEncoding (selectedLevel)
open WordEncoding (construct)

/-- A uniform deterministic RAM constructs the precise family in linear output time. -/
axiom linear_time : ∃ (program : Program) (timeConstant wordConstant : ℕ),
  0 < timeConstant ∧ 0 < wordConstant ∧
  ∀ (n w : ℕ),
    wordConstant * (order (selectedLevel n) + 1) ≤ 2 ^ w →
    ∃ t ≤ timeConstant * (order (selectedLevel n) + 1),
      RunsTo w program [n] (construct n) t

end Lax920634.LinearConstruction

statements.signature:
linear_time : Exists fun program =>
  Exists fun timeConstant =>
    Exists fun wordConstant =>
      And (instLTNat.lt 0 timeConstant)
        (And (instLTNat.lt 0 wordConstant)
          (∀ (n w : Nat),
            instLENat.le
                (instHMul.hMul wordConstant
                  (instHAdd.hAdd (Lax920634.ZigZagConstruction.order (Lax920634.GraphEncoding.selectedLevel n)) 1))
                (instHPow.hPow 2 w) →
              Exists fun t =>
                And
                  (instLENat.le t
                    (instHMul.hMul timeConstant
                      (instHAdd.hAdd (Lax920634.ZigZagConstruction.order (Lax920634.GraphEncoding.selectedLevel n)) 1)))
                  (Lax808846.Ram.RunsTo w program (List.cons n List.nil) (Lax920634.WordEncoding.construct n) t)))
statements.doc: A uniform deterministic RAM constructs the precise family in linear output time.

concepts.title: Path Replacement Preserves Uniform Expansion
concepts.description:
Suppose a degree-$d$ regular port involution has at least a quarter of the
degree times the smaller cut side in boundary darts, and $d\ge2$.
Replacing its vertex clouds by paths gives edge expansion at least $1/(8d)$.

Full clouds of a cut form a small base set. Each partial cloud contributes
a distinct crossing path edge. The base edges leaving full clouds either
cross the final cut or reach partial clouds. Counting these two possibilities
bounds the size of the cut by $8d$ times its edge boundary.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The base cut counts darts to preserve multigraph multiplicity. The target is
a simple graph; the argument tolerates loops and overlaps between matching
edges and path edges.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax920634.PathReplacement

/-!
---
title: Path Replacement Preserves Uniform Expansion
type: lemma
---
Suppose a degree-$d$ regular port involution has at least a quarter of the
degree times the smaller cut side in boundary darts, and $d\ge2$.
Replacing its vertex clouds by paths gives edge expansion at least $1/(8d)$.

Full clouds of a cut form a small base set. Each partial cloud contributes
a distinct crossing path edge. The base edges leaving full clouds either
cross the final cut or reach partial clouds. Counting these two possibilities
bounds the size of the cut by $8d$ times its edge boundary.

# Formalization notes

The base cut counts darts to preserve multigraph multiplicity. The target is
a simple graph; the argument tolerates loops and overlaps between matching
edges and path edges.
-/

namespace Lax920634.PathExpansion

open PathReplacement EdgeExpansion Function

/-- An expanding regular port involution yields a uniformly expanding path replacement. -/
axiom replacement_expansion {n d : ℕ} (R : Fin n × Fin d → Fin n × Fin d)
    (hR : Involutive R) (hd : 2 ≤ d)
    (hbase : ∀ U : Set (Fin n),
      d * min U.ncard (n - U.ncard) ≤ 4 * (baseCut R U).ncard) :
  HasEdgeExpansionAtLeast (graph R) (1 / (8 * (d : ℚ)))

end Lax920634.PathExpansion

statements.signature:
replacement_expansion : ∀ {n d : Nat} (R : Prod (Fin n) (Fin d) → Prod (Fin n) (Fin d)),
  Function.Involutive R →
    instLENat.le 2 d →
      (∀ (U : Set (Fin n)),
          instLENat.le (instHMul.hMul d (instMinNat.min U.ncard (instHSub.hSub n U.ncard)))
            (instHMul.hMul 4 (Lax920634.PathReplacement.baseCut R U).ncard)) →
        Lax920634.EdgeExpansion.HasEdgeExpansionAtLeast (Lax920634.PathReplacement.graph R)
          (instHDiv.hDiv 1 (instHMul.hMul 8 d.cast))
statements.doc: An expanding regular port involution yields a uniformly expanding path replacement.

concepts.title: Path Replacement of a Regular Multigraph
concepts.description:
Replace every vertex of a degree-$d$ multigraph by a path of $d$ ports,
then join ports paired by the edge-reversing involution. Every port has at
most two path neighbors and one neighbor across an original edge. The
resulting simple graph is subcubic.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The port map need not pair distinct ports; loops and repeated edges in the
base graph are allowed. The undirected closure removes any loops and
identifies coincident edges. Base cut cardinalities count darts, preserving
the base multiplicities. Each crossing base edge has one source-side dart.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax920634.EdgeExpansion

/-!
---
title: Path Replacement of a Regular Multigraph
type: definition
---
Replace every vertex of a degree-$d$ multigraph by a path of $d$ ports,
then join ports paired by the edge-reversing involution. Every port has at
most two path neighbors and one neighbor across an original edge. The
resulting simple graph is subcubic.

# Formalization notes

The port map need not pair distinct ports; loops and repeated edges in the
base graph are allowed. The undirected closure removes any loops and
identifies coincident edges. Base cut cardinalities count darts, preserving
the base multiplicities. Each crossing base edge has one source-side dart.
-/

namespace Lax920634.PathReplacement

/-- Replace each base vertex by a path of its ports and add the paired-port edges. -/
def graph {n d : ℕ} (R : Fin n × Fin d → Fin n × Fin d) :
    SimpleGraph (Fin n × Fin d) :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel (fun u v =>
    (u.1 = v.1 ∧ u.2.val + 1 = v.2.val) ∨ v = R u)

/-- Base boundary darts with source in `S` and target outside `S`. -/
def baseCut {n d : ℕ} (R : Fin n × Fin d → Fin n × Fin d)
    (S : Set (Fin n)) : Set (Fin n × Fin d) :=
  {p | p.1 ∈ S ∧ (R p).1 ∉ S}

end Lax920634.PathReplacement

concepts.title: The Explicit Construction Runs in Polynomial Time
concepts.description:
The specified graph-table constructor is computed by one deterministic
Turing machine in polynomial time in the unary requested order. Its output
is exactly the graph encoding defined by the seed scan, tower recurrence,
level selector, and path replacement.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The model is mathlib's deterministic finite stack-machine model, with the
identity encoding on binary input and output words. Its polynomial bound
counts machine transitions. The theorem concerns the actual specified
function, rather than an arbitrary constructor of graphs with similar
properties. Fixed seed precomputation contributes a constant independent
of the requested order.

concepts.sourceText:

import Mathlib.Computability.TuringMachine.Computable

Turing machine in polynomial time in the unary requested order. Its output
is exactly the graph encoding defined by the seed scan, tower recurrence,
level selector, and path replacement.

# Formalization notes

The model is mathlib's deterministic finite stack-machine model, with the
identity encoding on binary input and output words. Its polynomial bound
counts machine transitions. The theorem concerns the actual specified
function, rather than an arbitrary constructor of graphs with similar
properties. Fixed seed precomputation contributes a constant independent

-/

namespace Lax920634.PolynomialConstruction

open GraphEncoding Turing

/-- One deterministic polynomial-time machine computes the specified graph constructor. -/
axiom polynomial_time :
  Nonempty (TM2ComputableInPolyTime id id construct)

end Lax920634.PolynomialConstruction

concepts.title: The Deterministic Seed Search Succeeds
concepts.description:
At every finite order the deterministic table scan finds thirty permutations
such that, for every set of at most half the vertices, some permutation
moves at least a tenth of that set outside itself.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The scan checks this exact decidable property. A finite counting argument
proves that a successful candidate exists, and numerical enumeration covers
every candidate. The total default in the constructor is never needed.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax920634.SeedSearch
import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Fin.Basic

/-!
---
title: Rotation Map of the Fixed Powered Seed
type: definition
---
The selected thirty permutations supply sixty forward and inverse darts.
Adding sixty stationary darts makes the walk lazy. Raising this fixed
120-regular graph to the power 5760000 gives a seed of degree
$D=120^{5760000}$ on $D^4$ vertices. Labels of powered edges encode their
sequences of original darts in base 120.

# Formalization notes

Every definition is executable. Finite inverse queries are computed by the
scan in `SeedSearch`. Powered edges reverse the traversed dart labels in
reverse order. The long exponent and seed size are fixed constants.
-/

namespace Lax920634.SeedRotation

open SeedSearch

/-- Number forward and inverse permutation darts by integers below sixty. -/
def permutationLabels : (Fin 30 × Bool) ≃ Fin 60 :=
  (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.refl _) finTwoEquiv.symm).trans finProdFinEquiv

/-- Number the permutation darts and the sixty stationary darts together. -/
def lazyLabels : ((Fin 30 × Bool) ⊕ Fin 60) ≃ Fin 120 :=
  (Equiv.sumCongr permutationLabels (Equiv.refl _)).trans finSumFinEquiv

/-- The rotation of the selected lazy permutation graph, with numbered labels. -/
def lazyRotation (n : ℕ) (p : Fin n × Fin 120) : Fin n × Fin 120 :=
  match lazyLabels.symm p.2 with
  | Sum.inl (i, false) =>
    (selectedTable n i p.1, lazyLabels (Sum.inl (i, true)))
  | Sum.inl (i, true) =>
    (inverse (selectedTable n i) p.1,
      lazyLabels (Sum.inl (i, false)))
  | Sum.inr j => (p.1, lazyLabels (Sum.inr j))

/-- Follow a finite sequence of numbered darts to its endpoint. -/
def walkEnd {n d : ℕ} (R : Fin n × Fin d → Fin n × Fin d) :
    (t : ℕ) → Fin n → (Fin t → Fin d) → Fin n
  | 0, v, _ => v
  | t + 1, v, s => walkEnd R t (R (v, s 0)).1 (fun j => s j.succ)

/-- The vertex reached after a prescribed number of steps of a finite dart sequence. -/
def walkAt {n d : ℕ} (R : Fin n × Fin d → Fin n × Fin d)
    (t : ℕ) (v : Fin n) (s : Fin t → Fin d) : ℕ → Fin n
  | 0 => v
  | k + 1 => if h : k < t then
    (R (walkAt R t v s k, s ⟨k, h⟩)).1 else walkAt R t v s k

/-- The edge rotation of a graph power, with dart sequences numbered in base `d`. -/
def powerRotation {n d : ℕ} (R : Fin n × Fin d → Fin n × Fin d)
    (t : ℕ) (p : Fin n × Fin (d ^ t)) : Fin n × Fin (d ^ t) :=
  let s := finFunctionFinEquiv.symm p.2
  (walkEnd R t p.1 s, finFunctionFinEquiv (fun j =>
    (R (walkAt R t p.1 s (Fin.rev j).val, s (Fin.rev j))).2))

/-- The fixed seed's rotation map, after lazy powering. -/
def rotation : Fin seedOrder × Fin seedDegree →
    Fin seedOrder × Fin seedDegree :=
  powerRotation (lazyRotation seedOrder) poweringExponent

end Lax920634.SeedRotation

concepts.title: Deterministic Search for a Fixed Expander Seed
concepts.description:
Thirty permutations of a finite set are sufficient to make every set of at
most half its size escape by at least a tenth through some permutation.
A seed can therefore be found by checking finite tables in numerical order.
This search is used at one fixed size, independent of the requested output
order. Its cost is a constant in the construction of the infinite family.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Candidate tables are numbered by their base-$n$ digits. The test is a
finite predicate about injectivity and cardinalities. The selected table
is the first successful candidate, with identity as a total default;
the correctness proof shows that the default is never needed.
The search is implemented by a finite list scan and uses no choice operation.

concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Fin
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Powerset
import Mathlib.Data.List.FinRange
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Find

/-!
---
title: Deterministic Search for a Fixed Expander Seed
type: definition
---
Thirty permutations of a finite set are sufficient to make every set of at
most half its size escape by at least a tenth through some permutation.
A seed can therefore be found by checking finite tables in numerical order.
This search is used at one fixed size, independent of the requested output
order. Its cost is a constant in the construction of the infinite family.

# Formalization notes

Candidate tables are numbered by their base-$n$ digits. The test is a
finite predicate about injectivity and cardinalities. The selected table
is the first successful candidate, with identity as a total default;
the correctness proof shows that the default is never needed.
The search is implemented by a finite list scan and uses no choice operation.
-/

namespace Lax920634.SeedSearch

open Function

/-- A table of thirty maps on a numbered finite vertex set. -/
abbrev Table (n : ℕ) := Fin 30 → Fin n → Fin n

/-- The number of vertices of `S` whose image lies outside `S`. -/
def escape {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n → Fin n) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : ℕ :=
  (S.filter fun v => f v ∉ S).card

/-- Each row is a permutation, and some row moves at least a tenth of each small set out. -/
abbrev GoodTable {n : ℕ} (T : Table n) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, Bijective (T i)) ∧
    ∀ S : Finset (Fin n), 2 * S.card ≤ n →
      ∃ i : Fin 30, S.card ≤ 10 * escape (T i) S

/-- The candidate table represented by a base-`n` integer. -/
def decode (n : ℕ) (code : Fin (n ^ (30 * n))) : Table n :=
  fun i v => finFunctionFinEquiv.symm code (finProdFinEquiv (i, v))

/-- All candidate codes in increasing numerical order. -/
def candidates (n : ℕ) : List (Fin (n ^ (30 * n))) := List.finRange _

/-- The first expanding permutation table found by the finite deterministic scan. -/
def selectedTable (n : ℕ) : Table n :=
  (((candidates n).find? fun code => decide (GoodTable (decode n code))).map
    (decode n)).getD (fun _ v => v)

/-- Find the inverse image by scanning a numbered finite vertex set. -/
def inverse {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n → Fin n) (v : Fin n) : Fin n :=
  ((List.finRange n).find? fun u => decide (f u = v)).getD v

/-- A fixed powering exponent sufficient for the lazy permutation seed. -/
def poweringExponent : ℕ := 5760000

/-- The fixed degree of the powered seed. -/
def seedDegree : ℕ := 120 ^ poweringExponent

/-- The fixed number of seed vertices, the fourth power of its degree. -/
def seedOrder : ℕ := seedDegree ^ 4

end Lax920634.SeedSearch

concepts.title: Arbitrarily Large Subcubic Graphs of Linear Treewidth
concepts.description:
For every size threshold there is a finite simple subcubic graph above that
threshold with treewidth at least its order divided by $48d+2$, for the same
fixed degree constant $d=D^2$. These graphs belong to the explicit expander
family.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The integer inequality $n\le(48d+2)\operatorname{tw}(G)$ expresses the
linear lower bound without division or rounding. The proof selects a large
enough graph to absorb the additive one in the general treewidth inequality.

/-!

title: Arbitrarily Large Subcubic Graphs of Linear Treewidth
type: theorem
---
For every size threshold there is a finite simple subcubic graph above that
threshold with treewidth at least its order divided by $48d+2$, for the same
fixed degree constant $d=D^2$. These graphs belong to the explicit expander
family.

# Formalization notes

The integer inequality $n\le(48d+2)\operatorname{tw}(G)$ expresses the
linear lower bound without division or rounding. The proof selects a large
enough graph to absorb the additive one in the general treewidth inequality.

namespace Lax920634.TreewidthExistence

open ZigZagConstruction EdgeExpansion Lax228581.Treewidth

/-- Arbitrarily large subcubic graphs have a fixed linear lower bound on treewidth. -/
axiom exists_subcubic_linear_treewidth (lower : ℕ) :
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), lower ≤ n ∧ IsSubcubic G ∧
    n ≤ (48 * degree + 2) * treewidth G

end Lax920634.TreewidthExistence

concepts.title: A Word-Sized Encoding of the Constructed Graphs
concepts.description:
A graph is encoded by its order followed by one matching endpoint per vertex,
in numerical vertex order. Consecutive ports in each cloud supply the path
edges. Thus the encoding has exactly one more word than the graph has
vertices. It determines the entire simple graph, including loop removal and
merging of coincident edges.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The row number determines the base vertex and port by division and remainder
by the fixed degree. This encoding uses machine words for vertex labels,
rather than unary coordinates. The requested order is supplied as one word.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax920634.GraphEncoding

/-!
---
title: A Word-Sized Encoding of the Constructed Graphs
type: definition
---
A graph is encoded by its order followed by one matching endpoint per vertex,
in numerical vertex order. Consecutive ports in each cloud supply the path
edges. Thus the encoding has exactly one more word than the graph has
vertices. It determines the entire simple graph, including loop removal and
merging of coincident edges.

# Formalization notes

The row number determines the base vertex and port by division and remainder
by the fixed degree. This encoding uses machine words for vertex labels,
rather than unary coordinates. The requested order is supplied as one word.
-/

namespace Lax920634.WordEncoding

open ZigZagConstruction GraphEncoding

/-- The complete matching table, with its graph order as a header. -/
def table (k : ℕ) : List ℕ := order k ::
  (List.range (order k)).map (matchingNeighbor k)

/-- Construct the word encoding for the same size selector as the binary constructor. -/
def construct (n : ℕ) : List ℕ := table (selectedLevel n)

/-- Decode the matching table at its declared graph order. Path edges are determined by row numbers. -/
def decode (n : ℕ) (tape : List ℕ) : SimpleGraph (Fin n) :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel (fun u v =>
    (u.val / degree = v.val / degree ∧ u.val+1 = v.val) ∨
      v.val = (tape.tail[u.val]?).getD 0)

end Lax920634.WordEncoding

concepts.title: The Word Table Encodes the Same Graph
concepts.description:
The word table contains exactly one header and one endpoint per vertex.
Its header is the graph order, every endpoint is a valid vertex label,
and decoding produces exactly the specified subcubic graph.

import Lax920634.WordEncoding

/-!

title: The Word Table Encodes the Same Graph
type: lemma
---
The word table contains exactly one header and one endpoint per vertex.
Its header is the graph order, every endpoint is a valid vertex label,
and decoding produces exactly the specified subcubic graph.

namespace Lax920634.WordEncodingCorrectness

open ZigZagConstruction WordEncoding

/-- The linear-size word encoding is complete, bounded, and faithful to the original graph. -/
axiom table_correct (k : ℕ) :
  (table k).head? = some (order k) ∧
  (table k).length = order k + 1 ∧
  (∀ j < order k,
    ((table k).tail[j]?).getD 0 < order k) ∧
  decode (order k) (table k) = graph k

end Lax920634.WordEncodingCorrectness

concepts.title: Explicit Zig-Zag Family and Path Replacement
concepts.description:
Starting with the fixed powered seed of degree $D$, square it. Repeatedly
square the current graph and take its zig-zag product with the same seed.
The level-$k$ graph has degree $d=D^2$ and $(D^4)^{k+1}$ vertices.
Replace every vertex by a path of $d$ ports to obtain the subcubic graph
$H_k$ on $N_k=d(D^4)^{k+1}$ vertices.

The rotation query below gives the construction directly in integer
arithmetic. Each recursive level makes two queries at the preceding level
and two queries to the fixed seed. Thus the number of fixed-seed calls is
$2^{k+2}-2$, bounded by a constant times $N_k$. Each integer manipulated has
$O(\log N_k)$ bits. Enumerating all edges is consequently polynomial in
$N_k$. The fixed seed search has an enormous constant cost.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The construction uses numerical vertex labels and the concrete deterministic
seed scan. The graph is the simple undirected closure of the generated path
and matching edges. The proof connects this executable recurrence to the
numbered zig-zag tower and verifies every returned matching endpoint's bounds.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax920634.SeedRotation
import Lax920634.EdgeExpansion

/-!
---
title: Explicit Zig-Zag Family and Path Replacement
type: definition
---
Starting with the fixed powered seed of degree $D$, square it. Repeatedly
square the current graph and take its zig-zag product with the same seed.
The level-$k$ graph has degree $d=D^2$ and $(D^4)^{k+1}$ vertices.
Replace every vertex by a path of $d$ ports to obtain the subcubic graph
$H_k$ on $N_k=d(D^4)^{k+1}$ vertices.

The rotation query below gives the construction directly in integer
arithmetic. Each recursive level makes two queries at the preceding level
and two queries to the fixed seed. Thus the number of fixed-seed calls is
$2^{k+2}-2$, bounded by a constant times $N_k$. Each integer manipulated has
$O(\log N_k)$ bits. Enumerating all edges is consequently polynomial in
$N_k$. The fixed seed search has an enormous constant cost.

# Formalization notes

The construction uses numerical vertex labels and the concrete deterministic
seed scan. The graph is the simple undirected closure of the generated path
and matching edges. The proof connects this executable recurrence to the
numbered zig-zag tower and verifies every returned matching endpoint's bounds.
-/

namespace Lax920634.ZigZagConstruction

open SeedSearch

/-- The fixed degree of each regular graph in the tower. -/
def degree : ℕ := seedDegree ^ 2

/-- The number of vertices in the regular graph at a given level. -/
def baseOrder (k : ℕ) : ℕ := (seedDegree ^ 4) ^ (k + 1)

/-- The number of vertices after path replacement at a given level. -/
def order (k : ℕ) : ℕ := baseOrder k * degree

/-- A total numerical query to the fixed seed's edge rotation. -/
def seedValue (p : ℕ × ℕ) : ℕ × ℕ :=
  if h : p.1 < seedOrder ∧ p.2 < seedDegree then
    let r := SeedRotation.rotation (⟨p.1, h.1⟩, ⟨p.2, h.2⟩)
    (r.1.val, r.2.val)
  else (0, 0)

/-- The regular tower's rotation, computed by squaring and zig-zag steps. -/
def rotation : ℕ → ℕ × ℕ → ℕ × ℕ
  | 0, (v, i) =>
      let p₀ := seedValue (v, i / seedDegree)
      let p₁ := seedValue (p₀.1, i % seedDegree)
      (p₁.1, p₀.2 + seedDegree * p₁.2)
  | k + 1, (v, i) =>
      let p := seedValue (v % seedDegree ^ 4, i / seedDegree)
      let q₀ := rotation k (v / seedDegree ^ 4, p.1 / degree)
      let q₁ := rotation k (q₀.1, p.1 % degree)
      let r := seedValue (q₀.2 + degree * q₁.2, i % seedDegree)
      (r.1 + seedDegree ^ 4 * q₁.1, p.2 + seedDegree * r.2)

/-- The matching endpoint of a port, in the canonical vertex numbering. -/
def matchingNeighbor (k v : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  let r := rotation k (v / degree, v % degree)
  r.2 + degree * r.1

/-- The subcubic graph defined by the explicit tower and path-edge formulas. -/
def graph (k : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (Fin (order k)) :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel (fun u v =>
    (u.val / degree = v.val / degree ∧ u.val + 1 = v.val) ∨
      v.val = matchingNeighbor k u.val)

/-- The candidate neighbors, omitting nonexistent endpoint edges of a path. -/
def neighbors (k v : ℕ) : List ℕ :=
  (if 0 < v % degree then [v - 1] else []) ++
    (if v % degree + 1 < degree then [v + 1] else []) ++
    [matchingNeighbor k v]

end Lax920634.ZigZagConstruction

proofs.description:
The output encoding is the rotation table of the selected tower member,
with each row interpreted as one path-replacement vertex.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Identify the numerical selector and bracket serialization with the proved
polynomial-time tower-table construction. Transfer its deterministic machine
through pointwise equality and the registered machine-model bridge.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown:
The zig-zag product is due to Reingold, Vadhan, and Wigderson. The tower-table
and machine-model proofs are reused from the registered Lax323828 development,
including contributions by Bolton Bailey and Samuel Schlesinger.

proofs.description:
Compile one fixed structured program that initializes the deterministic seed,
materializes successive rotation tables, and prints the complete final table.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Each new row uses the exact zig-zag recurrence with indexed accesses to the
fixed seed and preceding table. The old tables occupy disjoint consecutive
memory blocks. A geometric potential pays for every growth stage. A final
linear scan writes one word per vertex and the order header. The verified
Lax808846 compiler bounds actual machine instructions and all physical
addresses at every sufficiently large word width.

proofs.description:
The bounded level scan reaches the first sufficiently large regular tower
member. The preceding level was below twice the request, bounding overshoot.
Select the first sufficiently large tower member, then use its proved subcubicity and uniform expansion.
Small components after deletion force a large deletion set. Connected sets containing more than half the vertices form a bramble, and tree Helly supplies a bag meeting every member.
The powered seed has spectral bound one fifth. Zig-zag iteration gives bound two fifths, and path replacement gives the stated edge expansion.
Apply the expansion-to-treewidth inequality to the proved degree and expansion bounds of the same executable graph.
Count crossing edges in partial clouds and base edges leaving full clouds.
A finite counting argument guarantees a good table; exhaustive numerical enumeration finds it.
Identify the executable graph with path replacement. Each port has two path neighbors and at most one paired neighbor.
Choose a graph of order at least twice the additive constant. Its treewidth is positive, so the additive one is absorbed into twice the linear coefficient.

The complete numerical row scan has the stated length and header. Its
endpoints agree with the original matching formula and remain in range.
Substituting these entries into the decoder gives the original graph.
